    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We sell
our products to mass merchandiser and food and drug retailers in the United
States. Consequently, our total revenues are affected by fluctuations in the
buying patterns of these customers. These fluctuations may result from wholesale
buying decisions, economic conditions and other factors. In addition, with the
growing trend towards retail consolidation, we are increasingly dependent upon a
few leading retailers, such as Wal-Mart Stores, Inc., whose bargaining strength
continues to grow due to their size. Such retailers have demanded, and may
continue to demand, increased service and order accommodations as well as price
and incremental promotional investment concessions. As a result, we may face
downward pressure on our prices and increased promotional expenses to meet these
demands, which would reduce our margins. We also may be negatively affected by
changes in the policies of our retail trade customers such as inventory
destocking, limitations on access to shelf space and other
conditions.</font></div>

manufacturer may force us to shift production to in-house facilities and
possibly cause manufacturing delays, disrupt our ability to fill orders or
require us to suspend production until we find another third party manufacturer.
We are not able to control the manufacturing efforts of these third party
manufacturers as closely as we control our business. Should any of these
manufacturers fail to meet our standards, we may face regulatory sanctions,
additional product liability claims or customer complaints, any of which could
harm our reputation and our business.</font></div>

laws of the United States.&#160;&#160;We cannot assure you that we will be able
to successfully protect our trademarks from infringement or otherwise. The loss
or infringement of our trademarks could impair the goodwill associated with our
brands, harm our reputation and materially adversely affect our financial
results.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
license additional intellectual property from third parties that is used in
certain of our products, and we cannot assure you that these third parties can
successfully maintain their intellectual property rights. In addition, the sale
of these products relies on our ability to maintain and extend our licensing
agreements with third parties, and we cannot assure you that we will be
successful in maintaining these licensing agreements. Any significant impairment
of the intellectual property covered by these licenses, or in our rights to use
this intellectual property, may cause our sales to decline.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
addition, our product line extensions are often based on new or unique delivery
methods for those products like our <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> patches and sleeves.
These delivery methods may not be protected by intellectual property rights that
we own or license on an exclusive basis or by exclusive manufacturing
agreements. As a result, we may be unable to prevent any competitor or customer
from duplicating our delivery methods to compete directly with these product
line extensions, which could cause sales to suffer.</font></div>

activities could have the effect of increasing, or preventing a decline in, the
price of our common stock.&#160;&#160;Such effect is expected to be greater in
the event we elect to settle converted convertible notes entirely in
cash.&#160;&#160;The counterparty to these transactions is likely to modify its
hedge positions from time to time prior to conversion or maturity of the
convertible notes or termination of the transactions by purchasing and selling
shares of our common stock, other of our securities, or other instruments it may
wish to use in connection with such hedging.&#160;&#160;In particular, such
hedging modification may occur during any conversion reference period for a
conversion of convertible notes, which may have a negative effect on the value
of the consideration received in relation to the conversion of those convertible
notes.&#160;&#160;In addition, we intend to exercise options we hold under the
convertible note hedge transaction whenever convertible notes are
converted.&#160;&#160;In order to unwind its hedge position with respect to
those exercised options, the counterparty to these transactions expects to sell
shares of our common stock in secondary market transactions or unwind various
over-the-counter derivative transactions with respect to our common stock during
the conversion reference period for the converted convertible
notes.</font></div>

of our convertible notes may dilute the ownership interest of existing
shareholders, including holders who had previously converted their convertible
notes.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

convertible notes may dilute the ownership interests of existing
shareholders.&#160;&#160;All or a portion of the amounts payable upon conversion
of the convertible notes may, at our election, be paid in cash rather than in
the form of shares of common stock.&#160;&#160;Any sales in the public market of
the common stock issued upon such conversion could adversely affect prevailing
market prices of our common stock.&#160;&#160;In addition, the existence of the
convertible notes may encourage short selling by market participants because the
conversion of the convertible notes could depress the price of our common
stock.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Virtually
all of our assets consist of intangibles.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As our
financial statements indicate, a substantial portion of our assets consist of
intangibles, principally the trademarks, trade names and patents that we have
acquired.&#160;&#160;In the event that the value of those assets became impaired
or our business is materially adversely affected in any way, we would not have
sufficient tangible assets that could be sold to repay our
liabilities.&#160;&#160;As a result, our creditors and investors may not be able
to recoup the amount of the indebtedness that they have extended to us or the
amount they have invested in us.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
products target niche markets that are often outside the focus of larger
companies where we believe we can achieve and sustain significant market share
through innovation and strong advertising and promotion support. Many of our
products are among the U.S. market leaders in their respective categories. For
example, our portfolio of topical analgesic brands, our <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Cortizone-10</font> anti-itch
ointment and our <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Gold
Bond</font> medicated body powders have the leading U.S. market share in their
respective categories. We support our brands through extensive and
cost-effective advertising and promotion, the expenditures for which represented
approximately 26% of our total revenues in fiscal 2008. We sell our products
nationally through mass merchandiser, drug and food channels, principally
utilizing our own sales force.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Product Recall</font></font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
February 8, 2008, we initiated a voluntary nationwide recall of our <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> Heat Therapy product.
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot </font>Heat Therapy is
an air-activated, self-heating disposable device for temporary relief of
muscular and joint pain.&#160;&#160;We recalled these products because we
received some consumer reports of first, second and third degree burns and skin
irritation resulting from the use or possible misuse of the
product.&#160;&#160;Based in part on consideration of on-hand factory inventory
and retail point of sales data, during the first quarter of fiscal 2008 we
recorded an estimate of approximately $6.0 million of recall expenses related to
product returns, inventory obsolescence, destruction costs, consumer refunds,
legal fees and other estimated expenses.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to our first
fiscal quarter, we increased our estimate of recall expenses by $0.3 million, to
a total of $6.3 million, primarily as a result of additional legal fees and
settlement payments.&#160;&#160;The remaining accrued liability for product
recall expenses was $0.8 million as of November 30, 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loss
on Early Extinguishment of Debt</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
the first quarter of fiscal 2008, we utilized borrowings under the revolving
credit facility portion of our Credit Facility to repay $35.0 million of the
term loan under the Credit Facility.&#160;&#160;In connection with the term loan
repayment, we retired a proportional share of the term loan debt issuance costs
and recorded the resulting loss on extinguishment of debt of $0.5
million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Stock
Repurchase</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
fiscal 2008, we repurchased 418,281 shares of our common stock under our stock
repurchase program for $26.3 million at an average price per share of
$62.94.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Litigation
Settlement</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
the third quarter of fiscal 2008, we reached a settlement on all 26 known claims
alleging pulmonary arterial hypertension as a result of the ingestion of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font> products in 1998
through 2003.&#160;&#160;Included as litigation settlement in the consolidated
statements of income is the settlement of the 26 claims totaling $13.3 million
and $0.6 million of legal expenses, which were partially offset by $2.6 million
of proceeds from the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font> litigation
settlement trust.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Subsequent
Event</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
December 4, 2008 we issued an aggregate of 487,123 shares of our common stock in
exchange for $28.7 million in aggregate principal amount of our outstanding 2.0%
Convertible Senior Notes due 2013 (&#8220;2.0% Convertible Notes&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Upon
completion of the transaction, the balance of the remaining 2.0% Convertible
Notes was reduced to $96.3 million outstanding. </font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Critical
Accounting Estimates</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
preparation of financial statements in accordance with U.S. generally accepted
accounting principles requires management to use estimates.&#160;&#160;Several
different estimates or methods can be used by management that might yield
different results.&#160;&#160;The following are the significant estimates used
by management in the preparation of the November 30, 2008 consolidated financial
statements:</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Allowance
for Doubtful Accounts</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">As of
November 30, 2008, an estimate was made of the collectibility of the outstanding
accounts receivable balances.&#160;&#160;&#160;This estimate requires the
utilization of outside credit services, knowledge about the customer and the
customer&#8217;s industry, new developments in the customer&#8217;s industry and operating
results of the customer as well as general economic conditions and historical
trends.&#160;&#160;When all these facts are compiled, a judgment as to the
collectibility of the individual account is made.&#160;&#160;&#160;Many factors
can impact this estimate, including those noted in this
paragraph.&#160;&#160;The adequacy of the estimated allowance may be impacted by
the deterioration in the financial condition of a large customer, weakness in
the economic environment resulting in a higher level of customer bankruptcy
filings or delinquencies and the competitive environment in which the customer
operates.&#160;&#160;During the year ended November 30, 2008, we performed an
assessment of the collectibility of trade accounts receivable and did not make
any significant adjustments to our estimate of allowance for doubtful
accounts.&#160;&#160;The balance of allowance for doubtful accounts was $0.4
million at November 30, 2008 and 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Revenue
Recognition</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Revenue
is recognized when our products are shipped and title transfers to our
customers.&#160;&#160;It is generally our policy across all classes of customers
that all sales are final.&#160;&#160;As is common in the consumer products
industry, customers return </font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">31</font></div>
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
          <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">products
for a variety of reasons including products damaged in transit, discontinuance
of a particular size or form of product and shipping errors.&#160;&#160;As sales
are recorded, we accrue an estimated amount for product returns, as a reduction
of these sales, based upon our historical experience and consideration of
discontinued products, product divestitures, estimated inventory levels held by
our customers and retail point of sale data on existing and newly introduced
products.&#160;&#160;The level of returns may fluctuate from our estimates due
to several factors including weather conditions, customer inventory levels and
competitive conditions.&#160;&#160;We charge the allowance account for product
returns when the customer provides appropriate supporting documentation that the
product is properly destroyed or upon receipt of the product.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
separate returns into the two categories of seasonal and non-seasonal
products.&#160;&#160;We use the historical return detail of seasonal and
non-seasonal products for at least the most recent three fiscal years on
generally all products, which is normalized for any specific occurrence that is
not reasonably likely to recur, to determine the amount of product returned as a
percentage of sales, and estimate an allowance for potential returns based on
product sold in the current period.&#160;&#160;To consider product sold in
current and prior periods, an estimate of inventory held by our retail customers
is calculated based on customer inventory detail.&#160;&#160;This estimate of
inventory held by our customers, along with historical returns as a percentage
of sales, is used to determine an estimate of potential product
returns.&#160;&#160;This estimate of the allowance for seasonal and non-seasonal
returns is further analyzed by considering retail customer point of sale
data.&#160;&#160;We also consider specific events, such as discontinued product
or product divestitures, when determining the adequacy of the
allowance.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
estimate of product returns for seasonal and non-seasonal products was $1.4
million and $1.3 million as of November 30, 2008, and $1.2 million and $1.3
million as of November 30, 2007 and November 30, 2006.&#160;&#160;Due to higher
sales volume during fiscal 2008, we increased our estimate of seasonal returns
by approximately $0.2 million, which resulted in a decrease to net sales in our
consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;Higher sales volume in fiscal 2007
offset by customers returning seasonal products earlier in the season resulted
in our estimate of returns for seasonal products remaining consistent as
compared to fiscal 2006.&#160;&#160;During fiscal 2008 and 2007, our estimate of
non-seasonal returns remained consistent as compared to fiscal 2007 and 2006,
respectively.&#160;&#160;Each percentage point change in the seasonal return
rate would impact net sales by approximately $0.2 million.&#160;&#160;Each
percentage point change in the non-seasonal return rate would impact net sales
by approximately $0.6 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">At
November 30, 2006, based on consideration of the sales of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot Pro Therapy</font>
performing below expectations, review of retail point of sales data throughout
fiscal 2006 and an estimate of inventory on hand at customers, we estimated
returns of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot Pro
Therapy</font> as of November 30, 2006 of $3.3 million, which was included as a
reduction of net sales.&#160;&#160;During fiscal 2007, we continued to monitor
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot Pro Therapy</font>
retail sales and inventory levels on-hand at customers and increased the
specific reserve for <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot
Pro Therapy</font> by $4.5 million as of November 30, 2007, which is included as
a reduction of net sales in our consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;As
of November 30, 2007, the allowance remaining for <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot Pro Therapy </font>returns
was $4.5 million.&#160;&#160;During fiscal 2008, based on a revised estimate of
inventory held by customers, we reduced the estimated remaining liability for
returns by $1.5 million, which resulted in an increase to net sales in our
consolidated financial statements.&#160;&#160;As of November 30, 2008, the
allowance remaining for <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy
Hot Pro Therapy </font>returns is $0.7 million.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
routinely enter into agreements with customers to participate in promotional
programs.&#160;&#160;The cost of these programs is recorded as either
advertising and promotion expense or as a reduction of sales as prescribed by
Emerging Issues Task Force 01-9, &#8220;Accounting for Consideration Given by a Vendor
to a Customer (Including a Reseller of the Vendor&#8217;s Products)&#8221;.&#160;&#160;A
significant portion of the programs are recorded as a reduction of sales and
generally take the form of coupons and vendor allowances, which are normally
taken via temporary price reductions, scan downs, display activity and
participations in in-store programs provided uniquely by the
customer.&#160;&#160;We also enter into cooperative advertising programs with
certain customers, the cost of which is recorded as advertising and promotion
expense.&#160;&#160;In order for retailers to receive reimbursement under such
programs, the retailer must meet specified advertising guidelines and provide
appropriate documentation of the advertisement being run.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
analyze promotional programs in two primary categories -- coupons and vendor
allowances.&#160;&#160;Customers normally utilize vendor allowances in the form
of temporary price reductions, scan downs, display activity and participations
in in-store programs provided uniquely by the customer.&#160;&#160;We estimate
the accrual for outstanding coupons by utilizing a third-party clearinghouse to
track coupons issued, coupon value, distribution and expiration dates, quantity
distributed and estimated redemption rates that are provided by
us.&#160;&#160;We estimate the redemption rates based on internal analysis of
historical coupon redemption rates and expected future retail sales by
considering recent point of sale data.&#160;&#160;The estimate for vendor
allowances is based on estimated unit sales of a product under a program and
amounts committed for such programs in each fiscal year.&#160;&#160;Estimated
unit sales are determined by considering customer forecasted sales, point of
sale data and the nature of the program </font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">32</font></div>
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center">
          <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="HDR">
        <div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right">
        </div>
      </div>
    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">being
offered.&#160;&#160;The three most recent years of expected program payments
versus actual payments made and current year retail point of sale trends are
analyzed to determine future expected payments.&#160;&#160;Customer delays in
requesting promotional program payments due to their audit of program
participation and resulting request for reimbursement is also considered to
evaluate the accrual for vendor allowances.&#160;&#160;The costs of these
programs are often variable based on the number of units actually
sold.&#160;&#160;As of November 30, 2008, the coupon accrual and reserve for
vendor allowances were $1.8 million and $4.9 million, respectively, and $1.9
million and $5.5 million, respectively, as of November 30, 2007.&#160;&#160;Each
percentage point change in promotional program participation would impact net
sales by $0.2 million and advertising and promotion expense by an insignificant
amount.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Income
Taxes</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
account for income taxes using the asset and liability approach as prescribed by
SFAS 109, FIN 48, FSP FIN 48-1 and other applicable FSP&#8217;s and FASB
Interpretations.&#160;&#160;This approach requires recognition of deferred tax
assets and liabilities for the expected future tax consequences of events that
have been included in our consolidated financial statements or tax
returns.&#160;&#160;Using the enacted tax rates in effect for the year in which
the differences are expected to reverse, deferred tax assets and liabilities are
determined based on the differences between the financial reporting and the tax
basis of an asset or liability.&#160;&#160;We adopted FIN 48, as amended by FSP
FIN 48-1, on December 1, 2007.&#160;&#160;FIN 48 clarifies the accounting for
uncertainty in income taxes recognized in the financial statements in accordance
with SFAS 109.&#160;&#160;In connection with the adoption of FIN 48, we
recognized an increase in the unrecognized tax benefits of $1.6 million, which
is included in the consolidated financial statements as a reduction to retained
earnings of $0.7 million and an increase to deferred tax assets of $0.9
million.&#160;&#160;We had a total unrecognized tax benefit of $2.2 million as
of December 1, 2007.&#160;&#160;Our effective tax rate was 33.7% for fiscal
2008, as compared to 34.5% in fiscal 2007 and 34.9% in fiscal 2006.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Accounting
for Acquisitions and Intangible Assets</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
account for our acquisitions under the purchase method of accounting for
business combinations as prescribed by SFAS No. 141, &#8220;Business Combinations&#8221;
(&#8220;SFAS 141&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Under SFAS 141, the cost, including transaction costs,
are allocated to the underlying net assets, based on their respective estimated
fair values.&#160;&#160;Business combinations consummated beginning in the first
quarter of our fiscal 2010 will be accounted for under SFAS No. 141R, &#8220;Business
Combinations&#8221; (&#8220;SFAS 141R&#8221;).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
account for our intangible assets in accordance with SFAS No. 142, &#8220;Goodwill and
Other Intangible Assets&#8221; (&#8220;SFAS 142&#8221;).&#160;&#160;Under SFAS 142, intangible
assets with indefinite useful lives are not amortized but are reviewed for
impairment at least annually. Intangible assets with finite lives are amortized
over their estimated useful lives using the straight-line method.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
judgments made in determining the estimated fair value and expected useful lives
assigned to each class of assets and liabilities acquired can significantly
affect net income.&#160;&#160;For example, the useful life of property, plant,
and equipment acquired will differ substantially from the useful life of brand
licenses and trademarks.&#160;&#160;Consequently, to the extent a longer-lived
asset is ascribed greater value under the purchase method than a shorter-lived
asset or a value is assigned to an indefinite-lived asset, net income in a given
period may be higher.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Determining
the fair value of certain assets and liabilities acquired is judgmental in
nature and often involves the use of significant estimates and
assumptions.&#160;&#160;An area that requires significant judgment is the fair
value and useful lives of intangible assets.&#160;&#160;In this process, we
often obtain the assistance of a third party valuation firm for certain
intangible assets.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Our
intangible assets consist of exclusive brand licenses, trademarks and other
intellectual property, customer relationships and non-compete
agreements.&#160;&#160;We have determined that our trademarks have indefinite
useful lives, as cash flows from the use of the trademarks are expected to be
generated indefinitely. The useful lives of our intangible assets are reviewed
as circumstances dictate in accordance with the provisions of SFAS
142.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The value
of our intangible assets is exposed to future adverse changes if we experience
declines in operating results or experience significant negative industry or
economic trends.&#160;&#160;We review our indefinite-lived intangible assets for
impairment at least annually by comparing the carrying value of the intangible
assets to their estimated fair value.&#160;&#160;The estimate of fair value is
determined by discounting the estimate of future cash flows of the intangible
assets.&#160;&#160;Consistent with our policy, we perform the annual impairment
testing of our indefinite-lived intangible assets during the quarter ended
November 30, with the most recent test performed in the quarter ended November
30, 2008.&#160;&#160;No impairment or adjustment to the carrying value of our
indefinite-lived intangible assets was required as a result of this
testing.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">In
January 2007, we completed the acquisition of the U.S. rights to five consumer
and OTC brands from Johnson &amp; Johnson (&#8220;J&amp;J
Acquisition&#8221;).&#160;&#160;The acquired brands were: <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">ACT</font>, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Unisom</font>, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Cortizone-10</font>, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Kaopectate</font>, and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Balmex</font>.&#160;&#160;In May
2007, we acquired the worldwide trademark and rights to sell and market <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">ACT</font> in Western Europe from
Johnson &amp; Johnson (&#8220;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">ACT</font>
Acquisition&#8221;).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Fair
Value Measurements</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
December 1, 2007, we adopted SFAS 157 as it pertains to financial assets and
liabilities, which provides guidance for using fair value to measure assets and
liabilities.&#160;&#160;SFAS 157 applies both to items recognized and reported
at fair value in the financial statements and to items disclosed at fair value
in the notes to the financial statements.&#160;&#160;SFAS 157 does not change
existing accounting rules governing what can or must be recognized and reported
at fair value and clarifies that fair value is defined as the price received to
sell an asset, or paid to transfer a liability, in an orderly transaction
between market participants at the measurement date.&#160;&#160;Additionally,
SFAS 157 does not eliminate practicability exceptions that exist in accounting
pronouncements amended by SFAS 157 when measuring fair value.&#160;&#160;As a
result, we are not required to recognize any new assets or liabilities at fair
value.&#160;&#160;SFAS 157-2 defers the date of SFAS 157 for nonfinancial assets
and liabilities and is effective in our fiscal 2009.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">SFAS 157
also establishes a framework for measuring fair value.&#160;&#160;Fair value is
generally determined based on quoted market prices in active markets for
identical assets or liabilities.&#160;&#160;If quoted market prices are not
available, SFAS 157 provides guidance on alternative valuation techniques that
place greater reliance on observable inputs and less reliance on unobservable
inputs.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Stock-Based
Compensation</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">We
account for stock-based compensation under the provisions of SFAS 123R, which
requires the recognition of the cost of employee services received in exchange
for an award of equity instruments in the financial statements and is measured
based on the grant date fair value of the award.&#160;&#160;The fair value of
each stock option grant is estimated using a Flex Lattice Model.&#160;&#160;The
input assumptions used in determining fair value are the expected life of the
stock options, the expected volatility of our common stock, the risk-free
interest rate over the expected life of the option and the expected forfeiture
rate of the options granted.&#160;&#160;We recognize stock option compensation
expense over the period during which an employee provides service in exchange
for the award (the vesting period).</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For
additional information regarding our significant accounting policies, see note 2
of notes to consolidated financial statements.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net sales
growth in the medicated skin care category increased $18.5 million, or 15.0%, in
fiscal 2008 compared to fiscal 2007 as a result of the launch of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Gold Bond</font> Ultimate Restoring
Lotion and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Cortizone-10</font>
Intensive Healing in the first quarter of fiscal 2008, the continued success of
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Gold Bond</font> Ultimate
Softening Lotion and our ownership of the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Cortizone-10</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Balmex</font> brands for the entire
twelve month period of fiscal 2008 compared to only eleven months of ownership
in fiscal 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net sales
in the topical pain care category increased $0.9 million, or 1.0%, in fiscal
2008 compared to fiscal 2007, principally due to increases in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Aspercreme</font>, led by the new
products introduced in the first quarter of fiscal 2008, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> PM Lotion, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> PM Patch, <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Aspercreme</font> Heat Pain Gel and
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Aspercreme</font> Nighttime
Lotion, offset by declines in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Capzasin</font> and the
discontinuance of shipments of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot </font>Heat Therapy
following our February 8, 2008 voluntary recall of the product. Excluding sales
of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> Heat Therapy
and<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic"> Icy Hot</font> <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Pro Therapy,</font> sales in the
category increased 6.9% compared to the prior year period.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net sales

ownership of the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">ACT</font>
brand for the entire twelve month period of fiscal 2008 compared to only eleven
months of ownership in fiscal 2007 and an expanded distribution
base.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net sales
in the internal OTC category increased $3.0 million, or 6.6%, in fiscal 2008
compared to fiscal 2007 as a result of our ownership of the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Unisom</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Kaopectate</font> brands for the
entire twelve month period of fiscal 2008 compared to only eleven months of
ownership in fiscal 2007 and the introduction of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Unisom </font>SleepMelts in the
second quarter of fiscal 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net sales
in the medicated dandruff shampoos category decreased $1.2 million, or 3.2%, in
fiscal 2008 compared to fiscal 2007 primarily due to declining sales of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Selsun </font>Salon, which were
partially offset by a full year of sales of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Selsun Blue</font> Naturals, which
began shipping in the second quarter of fiscal 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net sales
in the dietary supplements category decreased $6.6 million, or 25.4%, in fiscal
2008 compared to fiscal 2007.&#160;&#160;Net sales of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font> decreased 36.9%
primarily resulting from increased competitive pressures in the diet-aid
category, a decline in sales of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim Max</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: sub; FONT-STYLE: italic">2</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">O</font> and increased returns of
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font> mainly from
several retailers discontinuing <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim Max</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: sub; FONT-STYLE: italic">2</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">O</font>, partially offset by the
launch of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font> Max
Daytime Control in the first quarter of fiscal 2008 and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font> Max Complex 7, which
began shipping in the third quarter of fiscal 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net sales
in the other OTC and toiletry products category increased $1.0 million, or 6.1%,
in fiscal 2008 compared to fiscal 2007 driven primarily by an increase in fourth
quarter shipments of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Bullfrog</font> as a result of
expanded distribution in key retailers and the early season shipments of
upgraded product formulas for the 2009 suncare season.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Domestic
sales variances were principally the result of changes in unit sales volume with
the exception of certain products for which we implemented a unit sales price
increase effective April 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">International
Revenues</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For
fiscal 2008, international revenues increased $1.9 million, or 6.4%, to $31.8
million from $29.9 million in fiscal 2007.&#160;&#160;The increase was primarily
due to favorable exchange rates that increased net sales approximately $1.5
million in fiscal 2008 and a full twelve months of ownership of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">ACT</font> internationally in fiscal
2008 compared to seven months of ownership in fiscal 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cost
of Sales</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cost of
sales in fiscal 2008 increased $2.6 million, or 2.0%, to $131.6 million from
$129.1 million in fiscal 2007.&#160;&#160;Cost of sales as a percentage of total
revenues was 28.9% for fiscal 2008 as compared to 30.5% for fiscal
2007.&#160;&#160;The decrease in cost of sales as a percentage of total revenues
was primarily due to the integration of manufacturing of certain of the acquired
brands from the J&amp;J Acquisition in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2007,
partially offset by an increase in fuel costs in 2008 resulting in higher
inbound freight expense.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Advertising
and Promotion Expense</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Advertising
and promotion expenses in fiscal 2008 increased $5.9 million, or 5.2%, to $118.1
million from $112.2 million in fiscal 2007 and were 26.0% of total revenues for
fiscal 2008 compared to 26.5% for fiscal 2007.&#160;&#160;The increase in
advertising and promotion expenses results from higher expenditures for
advertising and promotion in fiscal 2008 in connection with the ownership of the
brands acquired in the J&amp;J Acquisition for the entire twelve month period of
fiscal 2008 as compared to eleven months of ownership in fiscal
2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Selling,
General and Administrative Expense</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Selling,
general and administrative expenses increased $4.7 million, or 8.1%, to $62.6
million from $57.9 million in fiscal 2007.&#160;&#160;Selling, general and
administrative expenses were 13.7% and 13.6% of total revenues for fiscal 2008
and fiscal </font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div id="PGBRK" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
      <div id="FTR">
        <div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left">
        </div>
      </div>
      <div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always">
        <div style="WIDTH: 100%; TEXT-ALIGN: center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">36</font></div>

          <hr style="COLOR: black" noshade size="2">

    </div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">2007,
respectively.&#160;&#160;The increase in selling, general and administrative
expenses as a percentage of total revenues was largely attributable to the
absorption of transition service costs similar to those paid to Johnson &amp;
Johnson related to freight and administrative costs that were recorded as
acquisition expenses in fiscal 2007 and an increase in fuel costs in 2008
resulting in higher outbound freight expense.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Product
Recall Expenses</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">On
February 8, 2008, we initiated a voluntary nationwide recall of our <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> Heat Therapy product.
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot </font>Heat Therapy is
an air-activated, self-heating disposable device for temporary relief of
muscular and joint pain.&#160;&#160;We recalled these products because we
received some consumer reports of first, second and third degree burns and skin
irritation resulting from the use or possible misuse of the
product.&#160;&#160;Based in part on consideration of on-hand factory inventory
and retail point of sales data, during the first quarter of fiscal 2008 we
recorded an estimate of approximately $6.0 million of recall expenses related to
product returns, inventory obsolescence, destruction costs, consumer refunds,
legal fees and other estimated expenses.&#160;&#160;Subsequent to our first
fiscal quarter, we increased our estimate of recall expenses by $0.3 million, to
a total of $6.3 million, primarily as a result of additional legal fees and
settlement payments.&#160;&#160;The remaining accrued liability for product
recall expenses was $0.8 million as of November 30, 2008.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Acquisition
Expenses</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Acquisition
expenses for fiscal 2007 reflect the costs incurred for transition services,
including consumer affairs, distribution and collection services, related to the
J&amp;J Acquisition.&#160;&#160;The distribution and collection services were
terminated in April 2007 and the consumer affairs services were terminated in
June 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Litigation
Settlement</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">During
the third quarter of fiscal 2008, we reached a settlement on all 26 known claims
alleging pulmonary arterial hypertension as a result of the ingestion of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font> products in 1998
through 2003.&#160;&#160;Included as litigation settlement in the consolidated
statements of income is the settlement of the 26 claims totaling $13.3 million
and $0.6 million of legal expenses, which were partially offset by $2.6 million
of proceeds from the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font> litigation
settlement trust.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Interest
Expense</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Interest
expense decreased $4.6 million, or 15.4%, in fiscal 2008 compared to fiscal 2007
reflecting a reduction in the principal portion of debt since August 31,
2007.&#160;&#160;Until our indebtedness is reduced substantially, interest
expense will continue to represent a significant percentage of our income from
operations.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Loss
on Early Extinguishment of Debt</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman"><font id="TAB1" style="MARGIN-LEFT: 36pt"></font>During the first quarter of fiscal
2008, we utilized borrowings under the revolving credit facility portion of our
Credit Facility to repay $35.0 million of the term loan under the Credit
Facility.&#160;&#160;In connection with the term loan repayment, we retired a
proportional share of the term loan debt issuance costs and recorded the
resulting loss on extinguishment of debt of $0.5 million.&#160;&#160;In April
2007, we utilized the net proceeds from the 1.625% Convertible Notes and
borrowings under the revolving credit facility portion of our Credit Facility to
repay $128.0 million of the term loan under the Credit Facility.&#160;&#160;In
July 2007, we utilized borrowings under the revolving credit facility portion of
our Credit Facility to repay an additional $25.0 million of the term loan under
the Credit Facility.&#160;&#160;In connection with the term loan repayments, we
retired a proportional share of the term loan debt issuance costs and recorded
the resulting loss on early extinguishment of debt of $2.6 million during fiscal
2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt"><br></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Income
Taxes</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
effective tax rate decreased from 34.5% in fiscal 2007 to 33.7% in fiscal 2008
primarily as a result of higher inventory contributions and an increase in the
statutory percentage used to determine the tax deduction related to domestic
production activities.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Net sales
growth in the medicated skin care products category was a result of the
acquisition of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Cortizone-10</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Balmex</font> in the first fiscal
quarter of fiscal 2007 (brands acquired in the J&amp;J Acquisition) and a 20%
sales increase of the total <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Gold Bond</font> franchise in fiscal
2007 as compared to fiscal 2006, led by increases of 35%, 19% and 8% in the
lotion, foot care and powder lines, respectively.&#160;&#160;The increase in the
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Gold Bond </font>lotion line
was led by a full year of sales for Ultimate Softening Lotion, which was
launched in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2006.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
decline in net sales in the topical pain care category was primarily
attributable to reduced sales of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot Pro Therapy</font>, which
was originally launched in fiscal 2006.&#160;&#160;Contributing to the decrease
in net sales was a $4.5 million charge for expected returns of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot Pro Therapy</font> recorded
in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2007, which resulted in lower net sales and
reduced gross margins.&#160;&#160;<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Sportscreme</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Aspercreme</font> experienced sales
declines of 31% and 9%, respectively, in fiscal 2007.&#160;&#160;This decrease
was offset in part by the launch of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot </font>Heat Therapy in
fiscal 2007 and a 7% increase in the base <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> business, led by the
launch in fiscal 2007 of the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> XL Back Patch and
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot</font> Vanishing Scent
Cream.</font></div>

    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The net
sales growth in the oral care category was attributable to <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">ACT</font>, which was acquired as
part of the J&amp;J Acquisition.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The net
sales growth in the internal OTC category was attributable to <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Unisom</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Balmex</font>, which were acquired
as part of the J&amp;J Acquisition.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
decline in net sales in the medicated dandruff shampoos category was a result of
lower sales of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Selsun
Salon</font> in fiscal 2007 when compared to fiscal 2006, the product&#8217;s first
full year of sales.&#160;&#160;The overall decline was offset in part by a 3%
increase in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Selsun Blue
</font>sales, partially as a result of the launch of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Selsun Blue Naturals</font> in
fiscal 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
decline in net sales in the dietary supplements category in fiscal 2007 was a
result of a 29% sales decrease of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font>, resulting from
increased competitive pressures in the category and the decline in sales of
<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Dexatrim</font> Max<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: sub">2</font>O after its
initial launch in fiscal 2006.&#160;&#160;Also contributing to the decline were
23% lower <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Garlique</font>
sales and a 33% decline in <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">New
Phase</font> sales.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">The
higher net sales in the other OTC and toiletry products category was due
principally to the introduction of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Bullfrog</font> Marathon Mist in
fiscal 2007.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Domestic
sales variances were principally the result of changes in unit sales
volumes.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">International
Revenues</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">For
fiscal 2007, international revenues increased $5.7 million, or 23.7%, as
compared to fiscal 2006, primarily due to the brands acquired in the J&amp;J
Acquisition and the <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">ACT</font>
Acquisition in fiscal 2007.&#160;&#160;Sales variances for international
operations were principally the result of changes in unit sales
volumes.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cost
of Sales</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Cost of
sales in fiscal 2007 increased $35.0 million, or 37.2%, to $129.1 million from
$94.0 million in fiscal 2006.&#160;&#160;Cost of sales as a percentage of total
revenues was 30.5% for fiscal 2007 as compared to 31.3% for fiscal
2006.&#160;&#160;The decrease in cost of sales as a percentage of total revenues
was attributable to an increase in sales of products with lower cost of sales in
fiscal 2007 as compared to fiscal 2006, offset by an estimate recorded for
potentially obsolete inventory related to our <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot Pro Therapy </font>line of
products.&#160;&#160;Based on our evaluation of the carrying value of <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot Pro Therapy </font>inventory
in fiscal 2007 and fiscal 2006, including a review of retail point of sale data,
on hand inventory and purchase commitments, a reserve was recorded for
potentially obsolete inventory of $2.5 million and $2.0 million during the
fourth quarter of fiscal 2007 and 2006, respectively, which increased cost of
sales in our consolidated financial statements.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Advertising
and Promotion Expense</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Advertising
and promotion expenses for fiscal 2007 increased $16.1 million, or 16.8%, as
compared to the same period in fiscal 2006 and were 26.5% and 32.0% of total
revenues in fiscal 2007 and 2006, respectively.&#160;&#160;The decrease in
advertising and promotion expense as a percentage of revenue for the current
period reflected higher advertising and promotion spending, as a percentage of
revenue, for <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Icy Hot Pro
Therapy</font> and <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-STYLE: italic">Selsun
Salon</font> during the fiscal 2006 launch period.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 27pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-STYLE: italic; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Selling,
General and Administrative Expense</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 36pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-FAMILY: Times New Roman">Selling,
general and administrative expenses for fiscal 2007 increased $10.9 million, or
23.2%, as compared to fiscal 2006 and were 13.6% and 15.6% of total revenues
fiscal 2007 and 2006, respectively.&#160;&#160;The decrease as a percentage of
revenue was attributable to increased revenue from the brands acquired in fiscal
2007 without commensurate increases in selling, general and administrative
expenses.</font></div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
    <div style="DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>
